story.title: Bitcoin's regulation bull case is played out. What could drive crypto gains moving forward - CNBC

facts.text: ARK Invest Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood told CNBC the investment management firm's $1.5 million bull case price target for bitcoin by 2030 still stands.
She also said that it wouldn't surprise her if bitcoin reached its all-time high again before the end of 2027.
The broader digital asset market has struggled after the Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill, failed to advance in the Senate in September.

"I think the biggest catalyst we're seeing right now is actually very much in motion and it's happening, which is capital markets are moving onchain," eToro CEO Yoni Assia told CNBC in an exclusive interview from the conference.
He pointed to the SpaceX IPO as an example, which had derivatives trading on eToro before the IPO.
That includes BlackRock , the world's largest asset manager.
Last month, Strategy's Michael Saylor said he thinks bitcoin's next bull market is already underway.
Wood said that ARK Invest believes bitcoin has found its low and stressed that cybersecurity is "top of mind right now," which could provide yet another opportunity for crypto markets to rebound.
Crypto investors are hunting for the next positive catalyst after U.S. crypto regulation — a longtime market driver — fizzled in 2026.
Assia said that supportive regulation in the U.S. from agencies, including the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, is also helping adoption of crypto.
